target_customer: Large contractors and construction companies in Brazil buying materials from many suppliers
problem: Contractors spend time managing orders, deliveries and payments across dozens of material suppliers.
business_model: B2B marketplace with take rate on construction material orders, plus delivery and payment handling

founders.name: Pedro Dellagnelo
education: Stanford Graduate School of Business, MBA ('16)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he led product and growth at early-stage startups before Oico.

founders.name: Pedro Rocha
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as former founder and CEO with no bio. Contxto (2020) and Bloomberg Linea (2022) both name him as a founder.

exit.reason: The company paused its original marketplace operation on 16 May 2023, citing the need for scale and capital that had become harder to raise, laid off about 70 percent of staff (about 40 people), and kept 15 people to explore a new model with remaining cash.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mainly marketplace and order-management software; the hard parts were operational (supplier onboarding, logistics, payments) rather than technical.

defensibility.rationale: Supplier and contractor relationships could build some stickiness, but sources show no data or network moat and the model needed heavy capital.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Bloomberg Linea (Jan 2022) says Oico does the same business as Mumbai-based Infra.Market, which also shares Tiger as an investor. No source says Infra.Market entered Brazil.

market_need_then: Brazil's construction purchasing was fragmented across many suppliers; Oico's 2020 coverage cites contractors' burden managing orders, deliveries and payments. No spend figure was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses oico.com.br with an English subdomain en.oico.com.br.

brand_strength.rationale: Covered by Brazilian startup press and Bloomberg Linea, but no brand pages, mascot or community evidence was found.

outcome_analysis: Oico raised a roughly 1.5M dollar pre-seed in 2020 and a 5.5M dollar seed in January 2022 from Valor, Tiger and others, then paused its marketplace in May 2023 and cut about 70 percent of staff. The company itself said the model needed scale and capital that were harder to find as markets shifted, so it could not fund the next stage; the unit economics label reflects the capital-heavy model the company described.
notes: Pre-seed is described as 8.5M reais by Bloomberg Linea and startups.com.br (about 1.54M dollars) and as 1.5M dollars by Contxto, so these are the same round. startups.com.br gives the seed as 30M reais. Competitor sources found are dated 2022 (Infra.Market), well after the 2020 batch, and the Aug 2020 Contxto piece named no construction rivals, so the list is empty. The en.oico.com.br site returned HTTP 503. The 2023 event is a pause and search for a new model, and YC lists the company as inactive.
